absent: Numeric values and semantics of sleepable sizing modes and size states plus boot list and workqueue identities
Layouts of sleepable control usage and per CPU data records plus counter bank organisation
Sequence handling and segmented callback list advance accelerate entrain and extract contracts
Module record fields for sleepable pointer arrays and notifier registration guarantees
Blocking primitives for wait queues completions mutexes and housekeeping affinity
Possible CPU iteration tick rate current time source and CPU online checks
Common callback queuing parameters and hurry versus lazy tradeoffs
Synchronous grace wait and barrier wait latency and sleep context constraints beyond what is shown
Flavour specific grace functions and task scanning predicates for task based variants
Stall detection usage and reporting paths beyond default threshold values
Ordering guarantees of single accesses and barriers beyond placement
Timer workqueue and interrupt work scheduling guarantees

findings.text: Boot initialisation chooses between fixed large sizing and contention driven sizing for sleepable read copy update structures using the configured automatic mode together with the possible CPU count and a large system threshold. It then marks initialisation complete and moves every entry from a boot time pending list onto the grace period workqueue, promoting small objects awaiting allocation when early sizing is active.

Provides a small blocking coordination object with four operations: initialise by clearing state and preparing a wait queue, enter by registering a reader and ensuring a grace period has elapsed, exit by deregistering and arranging a later transition to idle, and destroy by collapsing any replay request and waiting until idle when necessary. Enter blocks until the passed marker is reached except for the first entrant which completes synchronously.

Offers a hurried callback request that forwards a callback record and handler to the common queuing path with urgency enabled rather than lazy batching. Callers use it when a state transition must be observed promptly, such as completion of a coordination grace period.

Exposes a snapshot and poll interface for grace period progress. Snapshot returns the current sequence value. Poll reports completion when given a special completed marker or when the current sequence differs from the snapshot, with the tree flavour additionally ordering prior grace completion before later accesses while the tiny flavour performs a plain inequality check.

Handles dynamic module arrival and departure for sleepable structures. On arrival it allocates per CPU reader state for each structure listed by the module and points the counter pointer at the first bank, failing the notification on allocation failure. On departure it releases static state when no grace is needed and frees per CPU storage when no readers remain. A statically allocated notifier block dispatches these two cases and an early init routine registers it, logging on registration failure.

Defines the asynchronous completion path for the coordination object. A helper queues the completion routine with hurried urgency. The routine itself runs after a grace period and, while holding interrupt excluding protection, either advances to passed and wakes waiters when readers remain, requeues through an intermediate exit state when a new exit raced, or returns to idle when no further work exists. Entry in idle or already passed states indicates misuse.

Runs grace handling for task based flavours in a dedicated thread that first prepares per CPU timers and urgency flags, restricts itself to housekeeping CPUs, then publishes itself with release ordering and repeatedly performs single grace iterations separated by idle sleeps. A single iteration waits for pending callbacks unless in early boot, optionally brackets a flavour specific grace function with sequence start and end markers, then invokes ready callbacks beginning at CPU zero. The synchronous wait primitive uses the thread when available and otherwise performs a direct early boot iteration, refusing to run before the scheduler is active.

Covers deferred invocation helpers. A timer rearms itself and requests a grace scan when its per CPU list is non empty and lazy batching is enabled, marking urgency. An interrupt context wake helper and a workqueue helper both funnel toward callback invocation. Invocation first spreads work to up to two successors in heap order when within the active dequeue range and online state allows, then extracts completed callbacks under per CPU protection and runs each with bottom half exclusion and a scheduling opportunity before accounting length and re accelerating remaining entries. A barrier completion helper marks its record invoked and completes the barrier when its count reaches zero.

Per CPU record holds callback storage in cblist guarded by private lock. Timing uses rtp_jiffies for last activity and rtp_n_lock_retries for contention. Deferral uses lazy_timer with urgency flag urgent_gp. Scheduling uses rtp_work for process context and rtp_irq_work for interrupt context. Barrier coordination reuses barrier_q_head self linked when idle. Task sets use rtp_blkd_tasks for blocked tasks and rtp_exit_list for exiting tasks. Identity uses cpu and index plus parent link rtpp.

Central control holds wait channel cbs_wait with global guard cbs_gbl_lock and serialiser tasks_gp_mutex. Progress uses gp_state with gp_sleep delay plus gp_jiffies timestamp and gp_start origin and tasks_gp_seq sequence with n_ipis counter. Thread pointer kthread_ptr indicates availability. Batching uses lazy_jiffies interval. Behaviour is parameterised by gp_func with pregp_func plus pertask_func plus postscan_func plus holdouts_func plus postgp_func and queuing entry call_func. Waiting uses wait_state. Distribution uses rtpcpu base with rtpcp_array index plus percpu_enqueue_shift with percpu_enqueue_lim plus percpu_dequeue_lim with percpu_dequeue_gpseq. Barrier coordination uses barrier_q_mutex with barrier_q_count plus barrier_q_completion plus barrier_q_seq plus barrier_q_start. Naming uses name with kname.

Construction helper defines one per CPU instance and one central instance for a named flavour. The per CPU side statically initialises its private guard and its interrupt work to the wake helper. The central side initialises its wait channel and global guard and grace mutex, wires the grace and queue functions, selects uninterruptible waiting, points at the per CPU base, sets lazy batching to a quarter second, records human and kernel names, derives the enqueue shift from the configured CPU maximum with both limits starting at one, prepares the barrier mutex, and seeds the barrier sequence well behind zero to tolerate early polls.

Grace processing is factored into six small roles sharing a common header dependency: overall driver taking central control, pre grace preparation over a list, per task examination taking a task and a list, post scan handling over a list, holdout recheck with retry flags and progress output, and post grace handling taking central control.

Coordination cycles through idle then enter then passed then exit back to idle, with an extra replay marker for races. Idle with no registrants moves to enter on first arrival while incrementing nesting. Entered readers sleep until at least passed. Completion after a grace moves to passed when nesting remains and wakes sleepers. Final departure from passed moves to exit and queues another completion. Departure racing an outstanding exit moves instead to replay, which the next completion converts back to exit and requeues. Teardown collapses replay to exit. Two misuse states are never valid on completion entry.

Task grace thread advances through a linear diagnostic sequence from initialisation through waiting for callbacks and for grace work, pre grace waiting, task list scanning and its post processing, holdout waiting and scanning, post grace handling, reader waiting, callback invocation, and final callback waiting. Each transition records the current time in ticks for stall detection and a parallel name table provides human readable labels in the same order for tracing.

Per CPU queues progress from enqueue through acceleration and advancement to ready and invoked. A periodic scan advances sequence numbers, accelerates new entries, and reports two need bits for pending grace work versus ready callbacks. Urgency is set by timers and cleared when empty or after lazy handling. When adaptive collapse is enabled, low total load first restricts new enqueueing to CPU zero while recording a grace marker, then after that grace restricts dequeuing as well, logging both stages. Invocation drains only completed entries and re accelerates survivors.

Barrier uses a sequence value with start and end markers plus a mutex serialised critical section. A snapshot that is already complete returns immediately after ordering. Otherwise the initiator records start time, initialises completion state with a base count of two, attempts to entrain one marker per active CPU queue incrementing for each success, then drops the base count and sleeps until the last marker callback completes. Each marker self identifies as invoked before decrementing and completing when reaching zero.

The coordination object reuses its wait queue guard as the sole protector for state and nesting count, aliased under a short name. All state reads for decisions and all updates to state and count occur while holding this guard with interrupt exclusion, using ordered single accesses for cross context visibility. Waiters sleep on the same queue and are awakened while still holding the guard during the transition to passed.

Each per CPU queue is guarded by its own raw guard taken with interrupt exclusion for list inspection, advancement, extraction, length accounting, and urgency updates. The central enqueue and dequeue limits with the enqueue shift are guarded by a separate global guard, taken only for collapse decisions and updates. Initialisation prepares each per CPU guard and list exactly once and leaves empty lists ready for later use.

A grace mutex serialises whole single iterations including waiting, grace execution, and invocation starting at CPU zero, preventing concurrent grace attempts for the same flavour. A separate barrier mutex serialises barrier snapshots and entrainment, allowing barriers to coexist with grace iterations but not with each other. Per CPU guards are held only for short list operations and never across grace waiting or barrier sleeping.

Once the sizing decision is recorded, the boot completion flag is set before any pending boot entry is moved. The pending list is drained to empty with each entry removed before queuing, so no boot entry remains queued twice and no new boot entry can be added after completion without following the normal queuing path.

Module arrival establishes per CPU storage and a valid initial counter bank before the structure can be used, reporting failure without partial initialisation beyond the failing index. Departure releases shared state only when no grace sequence is pending and static storage is present, and releases per CPU storage only when no active readers are observed, warning otherwise.

Nesting count is zero exactly when idle outside transitions. The first entrant observes idle, records enter, and becomes responsible for synchronous completion. Later entrants only increment and sleep. Completion observes either positive nesting to advance toward passed, or zero nesting with replay or exit history to decide between requeue and idle. The final exiter is solely responsible for triggering exit work.

Destruction requires no active registrants and must not observe the passed marker. Any pending replay indication is normalised to exit before deciding to wait. Waiting occurs only when the current marker is not idle and success is defined as observing idle afterwards.

Enqueue and dequeue limits start at one and the shift is derived from the possible CPU count divided by the limit, rounded up when the division leaves a remainder. Negative configuration selects adaptive mode with limit one, while zero is normalised to one. Collapse to CPU zero proceeds in two grace separated stages and completion asserts that no callbacks remain outside CPU zero.

Urgency is meaningful only when lazy batching is enabled and the per CPU list is non empty. Timers set urgency and rearm for the next lazy deadline whenever those conditions hold. Scanning consumes urgency one level per pass when pending work exists and clears it when the list becomes empty, ensuring timers do not spin once drained.

Every grace state change records the current tick time for stall accounting. The worker thread publishes its own pointer with release ordering only after timers and urgency are prepared and affinity is set, so observers seeing a non null pointer can safely use the thread based wait path. Early boot and pre scheduler callers fall back to direct iteration or warn and return.

A reserved completed marker is treated as already finished by both tiny and tree poll variants regardless of current progress. Otherwise tiny compares for inequality while tree checks exact sequence completion with ordering that places grace completion before later accesses. Snapshot values are plain sequence reads without side effects.

Misuse is signalled with one time warnings rather than silent corruption: allocation failure on module arrival, residual readers or unexpected static state on departure, completion invoked from idle or already passed states, entry or exit with inconsistent nesting, and destruction while registrants remain or while in passed state. These checks identify lifecycle violations without correcting them.

Failure to allocate the per CPU pointer array is fatal to initialisation. Leftover callbacks outside CPU zero after collapse completion indicate a queuing error. Synchronous waiting before scheduler activation warns and returns without waiting. Timer and work paths assume their parent links and central control remain valid for the lifetime of the flavour.

Grace iterations may sleep waiting for callbacks, for grace completion, and for idle backoff, and must not be invoked from contexts that forbid sleeping except for the early boot direct path. Barriers sleep until all entrained markers complete and rely on mutual exclusion to prevent overlapping barrier attempts from corrupting the shared count and completion.

Coordination markers are small integers starting at zero for idle, then one for enter, two for passed, three for exit, and four for replay, preserving order so that at least passed can be tested with a single comparison. Short name rss_lock denotes the lock member of wait queue member gp_wait.

Diagnostic markers use integer zero for RTGS_INIT, one for RTGS_WAIT_WAIT_CBS, two for RTGS_WAIT_GP, three for RTGS_PRE_WAIT_GP, four for RTGS_SCAN_TASKLIST, five for RTGS_POST_SCAN_TASKLIST, six for RTGS_WAIT_SCAN_HOLDOUTS, seven for RTGS_SCAN_HOLDOUTS, eight for RTGS_POST_GP, nine for RTGS_WAIT_READERS, ten for RTGS_INVOKE_CBS, and eleven for RTGS_WAIT_CBS. A parallel table holds matching labels in the same order.

Stall policy uses thirty seconds for boot, ten minutes for runtime default with multiplier three for repeated reports, and ten seconds for info level. Callback tuning defaults to automatic enqueue selection indicated by negative one, contention threshold one hundred, collapse threshold ten, and lazy batch threshold thirty two. Adaptive adjustment starts cleared and is enabled when automatic mode is detected during initialisation. Lazy batching defaults to a quarter second. Initial enqueue and dequeue limits are one with shift derived as base two logarithm of the configured CPU maximum. Barrier sequence seeds fifty units behind zero to absorb early polls. CPU identifier count is populated during initialisation.
